events.event: Japan average cash earnings and household spending (June)
events.previous: nominal wages +3.2% y/y, real wages +1.4% y/y, household spending -0.4% y/y real (May)
events.description: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's monthly wage survey alongside the household spending report. The Bank of Japan watches wage growth closely as the key input into whether consumption can sustainably support the inflation outlook, particularly after the Bank held rates on 31 July.

events.event: Fed Governor Lisa Cook speaks on the economic outlook
events.description: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook addresses the Anchorage Economic Development Corporation's 2026 Economic Luncheon in Alaska. As a sitting voting member of the FOMC, her remarks on inflation, employment and the policy outlook are watched for signals on where she sits relative to the hawkish dissenters from July's meeting.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' measure of the gap between exports and imports of goods. A wider surplus is generally supportive for the Australian dollar, and the release is watched closely given China's status as Australia's largest trading partner.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's quarterly survey of businesses' and forecasters' expectations for inflation over the next two years. A rise in expectations reinforces the case for a firmer policy stance, and a high reading is generally supportive for the New Zealand dollar.

A monthly gauge of UK house prices based on Lloyds Banking Group's own mortgage approvals data, formerly published under the Halifax name and rebranded as the Lloyds House Price Index from July 2026 onward with the same underlying methodology. Read alongside the Nationwide index as a proxy for household wealth and confidence, which feeds into the Bank of England's broader view of consumer demand.

SECO's monthly count of registered jobseekers as a share of the labour force. Switzerland's jobless rate has been drifting higher through 2026 as the export sector feels the pinch from a strong franc and soft external demand; a further increase would add to the case for the SNB to keep policy loose when it next meets in September.

The European Central Bank's regular bulletin setting out the economic and monetary analysis behind its latest policy decisions. Not a policy event in itself, but can move the euro at the margin if it contains fresh staff commentary on the inflation or growth outlook.

S&P Global's survey of activity in the UK construction sector. Housebuilding has been the weakest part of the industry recently, with June's reading barely above May's six year low, so this is watched for signs of whether that drag is easing. Typically a minor mover for sterling.

The main measure of consumer spending across the Eurozone. A high reading strengthens the euro, while a low one weakens it, since consumer demand is a key input into the ECB's growth and inflation outlook.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics' preliminary estimate of non-farm business sector productivity and unit labour costs for the second quarter. The Fed watches this as a gauge of how much wage growth is being absorbed by efficiency gains rather than feeding through to inflation.

The number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time that week. A high frequency, early read on the US labour market, usually a minor mover unless it deviates sharply from expectations, and watched closely this week just a day ahead of the July jobs report.
The final reading of stock levels held by US wholesalers, a minor input into later GDP revisions. Rarely a market mover on its own.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem discusses the economic outlook and monetary policy. As a regional Fed president speaking days after the FOMC's unusually hawkish three way dissent at July's meeting, his remarks are watched for whether he leans toward that camp or toward the majority who voted to hold.

China customs data on the gap between exports and imports, usually released without a fixed time in the first week of the month. June's surplus was the second largest on record, driven by surging chip and AI data centre hardware related exports; the release is watched for whether that export strength has been sustained into July, with knock on relevance for the Australian and New Zealand dollars.

The Cabinet Office's composite gauge of indicators, such as job offers and stock prices, designed to signal the direction of the Japanese economy a few months ahead. A useful but rarely market moving cross check on the broader growth picture the Bank of Japan is watching.

The Japan Machine Tool Builders' Association's early estimate of new orders for machine tools, a proxy for capital spending intentions in the manufacturing sector both at home and among export customers such as China. A niche but closely watched gauge of global industrial demand.

events.event: German industrial production and trade balance (June)
events.description: Destatis figures on output from Germany's factories and mines, released alongside the trade balance. As the Eurozone's largest economy and biggest exporter, German industrial data is watched as a bellwether for the currency bloc's manufacturing recovery and for how tariff related trade frictions are showing up in the numbers.

events.event: Canada Labour Force Survey: employment and unemployment rate (July)
events.description: Statistics Canada's monthly labour market report, covering the change in employment and the jobless rate. Released alongside the US jobs report, it is watched for signs of how much slack is building in the Canadian economy while the Bank of Canada remains on hold until its next meeting in September.

events.event: US Nonfarm Payrolls, average hourly earnings and unemployment rate (July)
events.consensus: around 80,000 jobs, +0.3% m/m earnings, unemployment rate steady at 4.2%
events.description: The US Department of Labor's monthly employment report, the single most closely watched release on the calendar. June's payrolls figure of just 57,000 was well below expectations and reopened debate about the timing of the Fed's next move; a second soft print in July would add to that debate, while a strong number would support the more hawkish tone struck by some FOMC members at July's meeting.

Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin comments on the economy, arriving just hours after the July jobs report. As a regional Fed president, his reaction to the data and his framing of the path ahead are watched for clues on how the Committee's centre of gravity is shifting after July's split decision.

The Richard Ivey School of Business's seasonally adjusted survey of purchasing managers across Canada, covering activity, employment, prices and inventories. A secondary release compared with the Labour Force Survey out the same morning, but still watched as a timely, broad based read on Canadian business activity.

The Federal Reserve's monthly measure of outstanding credit card and other consumer borrowing. Watched for a gradual slowdown as a sign of how stretched US household finances have become after several years of high borrowing costs, though it is typically a low impact release.

A monthly survey of roughly a thousand investors and analysts gauging both current conditions and expectations for the Eurozone economy. Released earlier in the month than the more closely watched ZEW survey, it offers an early, sentiment based read on the currency bloc's growth outlook, though it is usually only a minor mover for the euro.

events.event: RBA interest rate decision and Statement on Monetary Policy
events.description: The Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Board decision, released alongside the quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy that carries the Bank's updated growth and inflation forecasts. All four major Australian banks expect a hold, though a still above target trimmed mean inflation reading has left a live minority view that the Board could tighten once more before its cycle ends.

Governor Michele Bullock's press conference following the rate decision. Traders parse the Governor's language on the inflation and growth outlook for hints on whether the Board still has room to raise the cash rate again or has reached the peak of the current tightening cycle.

events.event: South Africa Quarterly Labour Force Survey (Q2)
events.description: Stats SA's quarterly survey of employment and unemployment, one of the most closely watched domestic releases for the rand given South Africa's persistently high jobless rate. The Q1 reading marked a jump to 32.7%, so this update is watched for whether the labour market weakness has continued into the second quarter.

The National Federation of Independent Business's monthly survey of small business sentiment on hiring, sales and pricing plans, usually released on the second Tuesday of the month. A useful cross check on the health of Main Street businesses, though typically a secondary mover for the dollar.

events.event: German Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, final (July)
events.description: The final, confirmed reading of Germany's HICP inflation figure, the measure used for comparison across the euro area and a key input into the ECB's policy thinking. It rarely diverges from the flash estimate, but as the bloc's largest economy, any surprise revision can move the euro at the margin.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics' inflation report, the most closely watched US data release of the week. Headline CPI has been reaccelerating in recent months as the conflict driven jump in oil prices around the Strait of Hormuz feeds into energy costs, keeping the Fed under pressure to balance its inflation fight against signs of labour market cooling seen in Friday's jobs report. A hot print would bolster the hawkish minority on the FOMC, while a softer one would support the case for the Fed to look through the energy spike and keep open the door to a near term rate cut.
